rationale: The buyer is a real, identifiable person — an ML engineer or startup CTO actively spending five-to-six figures monthly on cloud GPU compute — and the pain (wasted engineering hours hunting Spot capacity across providers) is recurring and operationally costly, giving genuine willingness to pay for a monitoring/alert service. However, the core product is a real-time availability tracker, which requires polling cloud-provider APIs (some undocumented or rate-limited), handling provider-specific auth, and continuous uptime — meaning 'Claude + a landing page' is not sufficient; the backend engineering is real. Operational autonomy scores low because keeping live availability data accurate demands persistent infrastructure Youval cannot ship in a week without code, making this a validate-then-partner/outsource-build scenario rather than a solo factory build.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a GPU Spot availability monitor: users subscribe to real-time alerts when H100 (or MI350/A100) Spot capacity opens up across AWS, GCP, Azure, Lambda Labs, and DigitalOcean. To build it without Youval writing code, the factory would need to commission a lightweight polling service (a simple cron script hitting public or documented provider APIs) via a freelance developer or a no-code tool like Pipedream/Make, then wrap it with a Claude-powered alert-summariser and a Stripe subscription page ($29–$79/mo). Sell by posting in the HN thread itself, the MLOps Slack communities (Hugging Face, Weights & Biases Discord), and targeted cold outreach to ML engineers identifiable on LinkedIn who list GPU infrastructure in their bio — outreach goes out only after Youval approves each batch. Delivery is automated (alerts fire via email/webhook when capacity opens); support is handled by a Claude-powered FAQ bot; Stripe handles billing. The recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing weekly delivery logs. Honest caveat: the polling backend is the hard part — without a developer or a pre-built API aggregator (e.g. SkyPilot, Vast.ai), this stalls at the infrastructure layer, so the first validate step is confirming a no-code or low-code path actually covers the provider APIs before committing.
notes: build_gates not met: buildability_with_ai (4, below floor of 6) and operational_autonomy (5, below floor of 7). The product requires persistent polling infrastructure and real-time data pipelines that exceed what Claude + standard factory tooling can ship alone. Stage capped at validate pending a confirmed no-code/low-code build path or a technical co-builder.
